1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Three separated-looking individuals with large tail distinctions, slow but evolving motion and a broad frame.
1.natural_language: Photograph every individual of the two listed species exactly once. Frame its whole fluke with the camera crosshair inside it, release the frame, then use the shutter. On each photograph, mark both outer tips and the central V and archive it. The sea shows unlabelled silhouettes. Aim the camera, then click a whole clear fluke in its live view to identify it without shooting. The sample reveals its species name and WANTED or OFF LIST status and adds its shape to the field key. Empty or unclear samples are safe to repeat. Species names are assigned anew each survey. Use this key to choose listed animals and avoid off-list photographs. Tail scars identify individuals; whales stay unmarked and keep swimming during inspection and photograph review. A clipped, covered, duplicate or off-list photograph ends the attempt. Misplaced landmarks can be corrected before archive. Submit Census complete after all individuals are archived. There is one four-minute survey and no restart or world-stop control. Solve only from screenshots and visible controls in the task webpage. Do not use code, scripts, automation, Developer Tools, console, debugger, inspector, network, source, DOM, page-state inspection, terminal, shell, Python, address-bar or URL/query edits, reload/navigation, browser extensions, external applications, or other hidden-state access. full.summary: Drag the camera frame on the water and release; press Space. Drag the three physical pins onto the photograph. Click a whole clear specimen in the live camera to identify it safely. Learned WANTED and OFF LIST species shapes stay in the field key.
